issues.description: Element: Animal constructor and name accessor methods. The problem statement (UML and task text) requires the Animal constructor and the name getter/setter to use protected visibility: the UML shows a protected constructor (denoted '#') and the task text explicitly states "implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility". The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares these members as public: 'public Animal(String name)', 'public String getName()', and 'public void setName(String newName)'. This inconsistency can confuse students about the intended access level for these members and affects the encapsulation/inheritance guidance in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility between specification and implementation. Preferred fix: update the solution (and template/sample code if present) so the Animal constructor and the name getter/setter are declared protected. Concretely, in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java change 'public Animal(String name)' to 'protected Animal(String name)', 'public String getName()' to 'protected String getName()', and 'public void setName(String newName)' to 'protected void setName(String newName)'. Alternatively, if public visibility is intended, update the problem statement and UML to state that the constructor and accessors are public and explain why public visibility is acceptable.
